The test image shows a soybean stem with a distinctive pinkish/lavender discoloration along the stem. Leaves in background appear mostly healthy. This pink stem coloration is the key diagnostic feature.

Top candidates: Phytophthora (stem rot), Fusarium (pink stem), Rhizoctonia (stem lesions). Let me check references.
Not a match - Phytophthora shows wilted brown plant. Let me check Fusarium and Rhizoctonia.
Not quite matching. Let me check Rhizoctonia which can show reddish-pink stem lesions.
Good match with Rhizoctonia - similar purplish-pink stem discoloration. Let me use my final view to confirm.

**Analysis summary:**

- Test image: soybean stem with distinct pinkish/lavender-purple discoloration along a section of stem, plant otherwise has green leaves in background
- Phytophthora: shows complete plant wilt/collapse — no match
- Fusarium (Dise_10): stem curl with browning — partial match but not the pink color
- Rhizoctonia (Dise_18): shows **purple/pinkish stem discoloration** — strong visual match to the test image
- Rhizoctonia (Dise_29): node lesion with tan/brown necrosis — less direct match, but confirms stem as affected part

The diffuse pink-to-purple stem discoloration on a still-standing plant with healthy foliage is characteristic of Rhizoctonia aerial blight / stem canker.
